newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada probes Wal-Mart move against Cuban pajamas.
newsitem.headline: Canada probes Wal-Mart move against Cuban pajamas.

text.p: Canadian government officials said on Tuesday they were investigating if Wal-Mart's Canada subsidiary broke any Canadian laws when it removed Cuban-made pajamas from its stores across Canada.
"It's under investigation," International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said in an interview. "It's at a very preliminary stage."
He said the government needed more information before it could decide if Wal-Mart violated Canada's Foreign Extraterritorial Measures Act.

The act penalises companies in Canada for adhering to foreign legislation such as the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which fines companies for doing business with Cuba. No Canadian company has ever been charged under the legislation, Eggleton said.

Wal-Mart withdrew the Cuban pajamas from its 136 Canadian stores last week after a complaint from customers in a store in Winnipeg, Manitoba, said Edward Gould, a spokesman for Wal-Mart Canada Inc., a subsidiary of Bentonville, Arkansas-based Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
"What do you do when you expose yourself to lawsuits on either side of the border?" Gould said in a phone interview from Toronto.
He said Wal-Mart was seeking clarification from its lawyers in the United States and Canada and from government officials in both countries.
"We've decided to remove the product from the shelves until we get this clarified," Gould said.
He said there were at most 100 pairs of pajamas in each of the Canadian stores. The product is one of 80,000 products sold by Wal-Mart, he said.

Canada and Europe have spoken out vigorously against the Helms-Burton legislation, which allows Americans to file lawsuits in U.S. courts against foreigners deemed to have benefited from property confiscated by the Cuban government since the Communist revolution in 1959.
